title: Trigonometry: Law of Sines for AAS and ASA Checkpoint
description: Show that you can solve oblique triangles with two known angles using the Law of Sines.

questions.question: In △ABC, side c is opposite which angle?
questions.explanation: By standard triangle notation, lowercase side c is opposite uppercase angle C.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 58°, ∠B = 40°, and a = 26. What is c to the nearest tenth?
In △ABC, ∠A = 43°, ∠B = 69°, and b = 19. What is c to the nearest tenth?
In △ABC, ∠B = 57°, ∠C = 81°, and c = 28. Which expression finds b?
questions.explanation: Match b with ∠B and c with ∠C: b/sin 57° = 28/sin 81°, so b = 28 sin 57° / sin 81°.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 47°, ∠B = 48°, and b = 30. Find a to the nearest tenth.
questions.explanation: Use the complete pair B = 48° and b = 30. Then a = 30 sin 47° / sin 48° ≈ 29.5.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 31°, ∠C = 47°, and a = 12. Find b to the nearest tenth.
In △ABC, ∠A = 35°, ∠B = 75°, and a = 9.6. Find b to the nearest tenth.
In △ABC, ∠A = 38°, ∠B = 76°, and b = 17. Find ∠C and side c to the nearest tenth. Show the angle sum step.
questions.explanation: The angle sum gives C = 66°. The complete pair is B = 76° and b = 17, so c = 17 sin 66° / sin 76° ≈ 16.0.

questions.question: Complete a Law of Sines solution: In △ABC, ∠A = 57°, ∠B = 84°, and a = 32. Find ∠C, b, and c to the nearest tenth, and include an angle sum check.
questions.correctAnswer: C = 39° because 57° + 84° + 39° = 180°. Use a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C. b = 32 sin 84° / sin 57° ≈ 37.5 and c = 32 sin 39° / sin 57° ≈ 23.7.
questions.explanation: The missing angle is C = 180° - 57° - 84° = 39°. Then b = 32 sin 84° / sin 57° ≈ 37.5 and c = 32 sin 39° / sin 57° ≈ 23.7. The angle sum check is 57° + 84° + 39° = 180°.
